items.text: Donald Trump reacted to the devaluation of Iran's currency by posting a chart on the Truth Social network. He wrote that Iran has had 51 years of bad behavior. The chart shows that the value of one million rials dropped from about one dollar and 11 cents in 2025 to nearly 53 cents in 2026.
Mehrdad Geryvani, a Tehran resident, was released from Evin prison on Sunday, 18 Mordad. He had been serving his sentence in this prison since 1402.

Bahareh Aghaei, a lawyer, has been detained in Varamin's Qarchak prison for over seven months and remains in judicial uncertainty. During this time, she has spent at least 15 days in solitary confinement and has gone on a hunger strike once. This detention occurred following the protests in December 2025.

Three cafes in the cities of Mashhad, Bojnord, and Birjand were closed. Some of these closures were due to non-compliance with mandatory hijab rules. This action is part of an ongoing wave of business closures across the country.

The head of the Baneh Construction Workers Association announced that over 50% of workers in this city lack insurance. Inflation pressure and insufficient wages have forced some workers to do overtime, migrate to Iraq, or engage in border smuggling. These conditions expose them to the risk of death and exploitation.

Experts have warned that any increase in gasoline prices could lead to a new wave of price hikes, further decline in purchasing power, and even increased unemployment, intensifying economic pressure on low-income households.

Morteza Pouraliganji joined Pakhtakor Uzbekistan as a free agent after his contract with Persepolis ended. He signed a contract with the club until the end of the year. Pouraliganji has experience playing for several domestic and international teams and has participated in the World Cups.

63 members of parliament protested against the government's resolution on the special committee for managing cyberspace and the expansion of Masoud Pezeshkian's powers. The representatives requested a legal and religious review of this resolution by the Guardian Council. They believe the government and Pezeshkian cannot create broad powers without legal authorization.

Hossein Aghaei says that Trump's policy towards the Islamic Republic has not changed, but the approach has. The US is not seeking a broad military confrontation. Washington aims to increase economic pressure to force the Islamic Republic to negotiate.

Asghar Jahangir, the judiciary spokesperson, responded to Abbas Araghchi's remarks about a security gap by stating that if he has information, it should be given to the relevant authorities. He added that the prosecutor's office will take necessary legal actions if needed. Jahangir also emphasized that espionage and infiltration cases never reach zero.

Hossein Aghaei stated that if the proposed mechanism for reopening the Strait of Hormuz is approved by the US, ship traffic will be under the control of the Islamic Republic. He pointed out ambiguities in the memorandum regarding the management of the strait and maritime services that could lead to new disputes. He also considered the repetition of negotiations, threats, and war likely.

Citizens have reported that despite prolonged water and electricity outages, their bills have reached very high amounts. This issue has caused concern among the public. More details are provided by Leila Saadati.

Melissa Redin's book reveals new details about Mohamed Salah's hardships and sacrifices. Hamdi Nouh, Salah's first coach, describes his efforts to improve and endure long daily travels. This journey was stressful and worrisome for Salah's family.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the President of Turkey, arrived in Saudi Arabia for a one-day visit. Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan are set to sign a joint defense agreement. According to this agreement, an attack on any one of the three countries will be considered an attack on all three.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the government has overcome the crisis of water, electricity, gas, and power plant fuel shortages with the help of the people and consumption management. These remarks were made amid ongoing power outages and the energy crisis. The interview was conducted with Roghieh Rezaei.

Esmaeil Kowsari claimed that Ali Larijani was killed in Israeli and American attacks. Larijani's family denied this claim and stated that he did not have a mobile phone. They are following up on the matter with the responsible authorities.

Videos show that the birthday of the martyr Amirhossein Hazrati was held at his grave. He was killed during the protests on January 8, 2026, in the Khalij Fars neighborhood of Tehran. The event has been reflected on social media.

Roman Gofman, head of Mossad, has removed two senior officials from their positions due to the failure to implement a proposed plan to overthrow the Islamic Republic. These officials include the head of Mossad's intelligence department and the head of the Iran section. The report was published by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.

Amir Hamidi said Donald Trump's goal was to prevent a large-scale war in the region. He added that Trump aimed to pressure the Islamic Republic to remove its control and supervision over international ship traffic.

Two prisoners sentenced to death for murder were executed in Ardabil and Dezful prisons. These two prisoners were convicted in separate cases. The execution of the sentences in these two prisons has been confirmed.
Shirzad Payanian, a citizen of Mahabad, was arrested by security forces on Monday, 12th of Mordad. He was transferred to an unknown location.

Mehdi Sarami Far stated that the internet infrastructure in Iran has fundamentally changed during the war and internet outages. Iranian citizens' access to the internet no longer follows global patterns. This was mentioned in an interview with Iran International.

UN special rapporteurs warned about the intensification of repression against ethnic minorities in Iran and called for an end to arbitrary arrests, torture, and executions of Kurdish and Baluch citizens. At least 24 Baluch and 22 Kurds have been executed in the past seven months. The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights stated that at least 56 political prisoners have been executed in the past four and a half months.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin stated that with the weakening of Hamas and Hezbollah, the Islamic Republic has increasingly relied on the Houthis in Yemen and proxy forces in Iraq. He also described the tripartite defense agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan as part of a new regional equation. This alliance, contrary to the Islamic Republic's perception, was formed to counter threats from Tehran.
A citizen stated in a video that he paid over two million tomans for oil, yogurt, and butter. He ironically said, "God bless it." The video was sent to Iran International.

A citizen reported in a video that the Zamrud market in Dargahan on Qeshm Island has been closed due to a power outage. The video was sent on Monday, 19 Mordad. The market closure was reported due to the electricity problem.

Esmaeil Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said the Caspian Sea Convention defines the legal framework for cooperation among littoral states and prevents militarization of the Caspian Sea. He added that the final decision on Iran joining this convention rests with the parliament.

The executive committee of the African Football Confederation unanimously supported the FIFA president. The Mexican and Argentine federations also backed Infantino and rejected any attempt to remove him without an official vote. These supports came after Infantino apologized for the controversial World Cup commercial rights plan.
Kiomarth Hasanbeigi, a citizen from Ilam, was transferred from the IRGC detention center to the prison in Ilam. This transfer took place yesterday. Further details are not available.

A citizen described his poor financial situation in Turkey in a video sent to Iran International. He protested his displacement from Iran due to the rule of the Islamic Republic. The video was sent to Iran International.

An interview with Mohammad Hossein Aghasi, a lawyer, was conducted regarding the situation of women prisoners and the gap between Iran's criminal policy and the Bangkok Rules. He points to issues such as denial of treatment, legal responsibility of prison officials, and different treatment of political prisoners. This interview was published in the Peace Line monthly magazine.

The Wall Street Journal reported that new US intelligence assessments indicate Putin may test NATO's resolve with a limited action against a member state. The newspaper also noted that arms transfers to Ukraine and ammunition consumption in the Iran war have reduced US stocks of certain missiles and air defense systems. Scenarios under consideration include cyberattacks and limited ground invasions, and the earlier US assessment that Putin would avoid provoking NATO during the Ukraine war changed earlier this year.

US stock markets closed lower on Thursday. Investors were simultaneously monitoring corporate earnings and developments regarding potential agreement negotiations between the US and the Islamic Republic. Optimism about a possible end to the war had previously helped set new records, but the market now awaits details of the negotiations.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Donald Trump, the US President, has ordered a new investigation into the disclosure of information regarding the Pentagon's dwindling ammunition stockpiles. This investigation focuses on identifying the source of the leaked information about the status of US ammunition reserves. This action comes after media reports about the reduction of the Pentagon's ammunition stockpiles following the war with the Islamic Republic.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Armed Forces Commander announced the start of a security plan to prevent a possible attack on Saudi Arabia. This move follows reports of Iraqi militias and Yemeni Houthis preparing to attack Saudi Arabia. Baghdad has emphasized preventing the use of Iraqi territory for attacks on neighboring countries.

Mohammed bin Salman and Emmanuel Macron discussed the latest regional developments in a phone call. They talked about ways to strengthen regional security and ensure freedom of navigation. No further details of the call have been released.

The US and Israel have successfully completed a joint missile defense system test. The purpose of the test was to update the interception operations of interceptor missiles. Defense cooperation between the two countries has increased following the war with the Islamic Republic.

Mark Carney, the Prime Minister of Canada, announced that he no longer trusts Gianni Infantino, the FIFA president. He described the concealment of the controversial plan to sell part of the World Cup commercial rights as a deadly managerial mistake. These statements were made a few weeks after the end of the 2026 World Cup.

Al-Hurra network, quoting an American official, reported that Washington will not accept any agreement regarding the Strait of Hormuz that requires obtaining permits, collecting fees, or ceding control of commercial vessel traffic to the Islamic Republic. The official stated that any temporary shipping route must be without permits, fees, or any obstacles to the passage of ships. These remarks come as the Islamic Republic has announced it is finalizing a bilateral framework with Oman, under which Tehran will oversee the entry of ships into the Persian Gulf.

Tracking data shows that ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has decreased due to the conflict between the US and Iran and security uncertainties. Despite ongoing negotiations to reopen the waterway, ship passage has not returned to normal levels. Windward company reported that only 12 vessels passed in the last 24 hours, compared to about 140 daily before the disruption.

Arash Azarmi stated that the Islamic Republic has not been able to achieve its desired impact on the oil market by closing the Strait of Hormuz. Arab countries are developing pipelines and alternative routes to reduce their dependence on the strait. The Turkey route is one of these alternatives.

Israeli security officials have identified drone attacks as a major threat. The Israeli cabinet is planning to impose strict regulations and ban the use of drones. This decision is due to concerns about explosive drones and escalating tensions with the Islamic Republic.

The US Air Force has begun withdrawing its refueling aircraft from Ben Gurion Airport. This move aims to maintain civilian flight operations and prevent disruptions at the airport. The transfer is intended to free up airport capacity for passenger flights.

The World Players' Union (FIFPro) strongly criticized Gianni Infantino and FIFA management over the controversial plan to sell part of the World Cup commercial rights. FIFPro called for fundamental reforms in FIFA's governance structure and legal participation of professional football representatives in decision-making. The statement coincided with the English Football Association withdrawing support for Infantino and UEFA threatening to boycott FIFA competitions.

A senior Saudi official told Reuters that Iraqi militias, coordinated with Yemeni Houthis and led by the IRGC, are preparing for attacks on Saudi Arabia. Potential targets include energy facilities, ports, and airports. Saudi Arabia has monitored the movement of drones and missiles.

The Saudi-led coalition announced that Houthi attacks on Najran city injured 11 civilians. The injured include Saudi, Yemeni, Egyptian, and Pakistani citizens. These attacks occurred amid rising regional tensions.

Trump told reporters that he started a very important action in Iran because Iran cannot have nuclear weapons. He added that oil prices have dropped to $75 and gas prices in some parts of the US have fallen below $2. Trump expressed hope that after the war ends, these prices will return.

Saba Alaleh, a psychoanalyst, warned about the increase in poverty and difficulty in meeting basic needs in Iran. She said that continued economic pressures can reduce individuals' sense of control. This issue affects family, emotional, and work relationships.

A member of Yazd City Council reported a shortage of educational space in District 4 of the city. The increasing child population and lack of suitable schools have caused problems for families. He emphasized the need to complete the unfinished school and develop related infrastructure.

Craig and Lindsey Foreman, a British couple imprisoned in Evin, ended their hunger strike protesting detention conditions and the cut-off of phone contact with their families. The protest aimed to improve detention conditions and communication with family. They stopped the hunger strike after some time.

Kheybar Khorramabad Club announced that a person who was posting political content on an official page of the club has been arrested. More details will be provided in an interview with Mehdi Rostampour.

This morning, during the national wrestling team's practice, the electricity at Azadi Sports Complex was cut off. The Wrestling Federation owes 22 billion tomans to Tavanir and had a one-week deadline to pay it. The federation stated that the debt of the sports complex to the Ministry of Energy was the reason for the power cut.

A citizen in a video sent to Iran International stated that due to the high prices of essential goods, they have been forced to buy bread on credit. This indicates increased economic pressure on people. The rising cost of food items has affected people's livelihoods.

Iraq's Ministry of Interior announced that illegal drones will now be considered terrorist. Baghdad has made legal registration of citizens' weapons mandatory until the end of 2026. This measure aims to monopolize weapons in the hands of the government.

Israeli forces have intensified the siege of Ali Al-Taher hill in southern Lebanon. About 40 Hezbollah forces, including some members of the IRGC, are trapped in this area. More details are provided in an interview with Mi Farhat.

Tractor club announced that ticket sales for their match against Paykan in the first week of the Premier League will start today. The match is scheduled for Friday, August 14, at Sahand Stadium in Tabriz. This move may indicate the return of spectators to stadiums in the new season.
Mohammad Amin Askani, the internal manager of the Sunni religious school Anwar al-Haramayn in Pashamag village, was summoned by phone to the intelligence office of Rask county.

MarineTraffic reported a significant decrease in ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz from 15 vessels on August 7 to 6 vessels on August 9. A total of 32 ships passed through the strait during this period, with traffic concentrated on limited routes. On August 8, the passage of high-risk and sanctioned ships increased.

A citizen stated in a video that electricity and water are cut off in the city and people have become poor. He asked the Islamic Republic what more it wants. The report highlights the difficult situation of the people.

A Ta'zieh performance was held at the Center for Political and International Studies of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Abbas Araghchi and a group of ambassadors and foreign diplomats residing in Tehran attended the event. An interview was conducted with Mansoureh Hosseini-Yeganeh from Iran International.

Security forces shot at Farid Ramazani in the Aryashahr neighborhood of Tehran on the evening of January 8. The bullet hit his right hand finger, and the 29-year-old fell to the ground. A tattoo of the imperial crown was visible on his finger.

Alireza Jahanbakhsh, captain of Iran's national football team, has joined the Dutch team Excelsior to play again in the Eredivisie league. He previously played for several Dutch teams and returned to the Eredivisie after a season in Belgium. Jahanbakhsh was the top scorer of the Eredivisie league in the 2017-2018 season.

The Russian Ministry of Defense announced that its drones destroyed the infrastructure of the Bogorovatie gas field in the Sumy region of Ukraine. Ukrainian officials reported at least five injuries and damage to several residential areas due to Russian attacks.

Ahmad Nadari, a member of the parliament's presidium, said the parliament must provide the legal basis for revenge and blood vengeance for Ali Khamenei. He introduced Mojtaba Khamenei as the personal heir of the Supreme Leader and emphasized that this issue should be pursued on personal, public, and legal levels. Nadari also stated that the Islamic Republic must strive in military, legal, and political fields to achieve this revenge.

CENTCOM announced that it continues the naval blockade of Iranian ports with more than 20 warships. This action coincides with the Strait of Hormuz crisis and a sharp decrease in ship traffic. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Citizens consider the approval of the Caspian Convention as part of the Islamic Republic's policies to maintain power. They believe this action harms the national interests of the country. Baharan Azadi reports on citizens' messages regarding this issue.

Russian officials announced that a Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Nizhnekamsk caused at least 13 deaths and 39 injuries. The attack targeted an oil refinery in Tatarstan. A video shows smoke rising from the refinery area.

Farid Ramazani, a 29-year-old man, was wounded by officers on the evening of January 8, 2026, in the Aryashahr neighborhood of Tehran. The government forces first shot at his right finger, which had a tattoo of the king's crown, and then shot him fatally.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, had a seven-hour meeting with Mojtaba Khamenei. They discussed issues including people's livelihood, market conditions, employment, housing, sanctions, and unity. Khamenei's most important advice was to maintain unity and cohesion.

Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Foreign Minister, explained the main points of the Mecca defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey to Abbas Araghchi. The agreement was recently signed and aims to strengthen strategic cooperation and regional security. The two sides also discussed regional and international developments.

According to official European Union statistics, in 2024 approximately four million two hundred thousand people legally entered member countries from outside the EU. Iran International's analysis shows that for every 18 legal immigrants, one illegal immigrant entered the EU.

Rahim Shilani and Azad Rasouli-Fard, two citizens of Bukan, were each sentenced to two years in prison in a case related to the purchase and sale of Starlink equipment. The sentence was issued by the second criminal court branch of Bukan.

In France, after weeks of widespread fires, the risk of fire continues. In British Columbia, Canada, a large fire has caused one death and displaced over 20,000 people. A state of emergency has been declared across the province.

The German government considered the latest US plan for Gaza an opportunity to advance the disarmament of Hamas. The German Foreign Ministry spokesperson noted the complexity of the plan and the presence of disagreements and unanswered questions. More details were provided in an interview with Ali Hassanpour.

Mohammad Taghi Neghdali, a member of the Judiciary Commission of the Parliament, called for the notification and implementation of the Hijab law by the Supreme National Security Council. He described women's optional dress as a "naked coup" and part of a "war." These statements aim to legitimize government intervention in women's dress and lifestyle and increase pressure for mandatory hijab enforcement.

Ali Motahari expressed certainty that Masoud Pezeshkian will not resign. Mohammad Baqer Kharazi stated that Pezeshkian has attempted to resign 28 times. Kharazi was summoned to the Special Clergy Court following these statements.

Mojtaba Khamenei appointed his military advisor to the highest security body of the Islamic Republic. Mohsen Rezaei warned about internal unrest. He is described as Mojtaba's arm for external and internal conflict with the people.

General Ahmad Vahidi was appointed as the commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps with the rank of Major General. General Ali Abdollahi was named Chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, and Kiomarth Heydari was appointed as his deputy. Hossein Taeb was assigned as the head of the Basij Organization.
Mojtaba Khamenei appointed six commanders in the Armed Forces Headquarters, the IRGC, and Basij. Ahmad Vahidi was appointed as the commander of the IRGC. Mostafa Izadi was appointed as his deputy.

Esteghlal Club reformed its cycling team on the anniversary of the death of Parviz Khosrowani, the club's founder. This move is described as a return to the club's historical identity. The club also highlighted Khosrowani's important role in the formation of Esteghlal.

Soheila Hosseini, a detained citizen of Mashhad, was released from Vakilabad prison after posting a 4 billion toman bail. This release took place on Monday, 19th of Mordad. Harana News Agency reported this news.
A man in Sari was killed by his wife through administering methadone pills. The suspect has been arrested by the police.

Mojtaba Khamenei appointed Hossein Taeb as the head of the Basij organization. Taeb previously led the Intelligence Organization of the IRGC and was a senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC. He is on the US and EU sanctions lists for human rights violations.

Donald Trump stated that representatives of the Islamic Republic of Iran have demanded compensation for damages from the recent five-month military conflict. In response, he demanded compensation from Iran for deaths and injuries caused by Iranian actions. Trump has ordered that this issue be firmly raised in future negotiations.

Javad Nodehi, a political detainee related to the December 1404 protests, has been in legal limbo in Sabzevar prison for over seven months. Despite bail being posted, he has been denied temporary release. He also has no access to his chosen lawyer.

The family of Lindsey and Greg Foreman announced that the two British citizens ended their hunger strike after about three months in Evin prison. The couple was arrested in January 2025 in Iran and sentenced to 10 years in prison. Their child said the parents decided to end the strike to regain their physical strength.

Italy seeks a more active role in the Middle East amid security and political crises. The Italian foreign minister emphasized the importance of Rome-Riyadh relations. Saudi Arabia was described as an essential partner for regional stability.

The Chief of Staff of the Israeli Army stated in a meeting with the CENTCOM commander that the army's historic achievements must be preserved and strengthened. He emphasized that the army is fully prepared for an immediate return to heavy combat. The CENTCOM commander also highlighted the strategic cooperation between the US and Israeli armies.

Donald Trump stated in a recent post that Iran should be held responsible for the damages and deaths in Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza. These remarks were made in the context of Iran negotiations. Trump made this statement one hour ago.

The Internal Affairs Commission of the Parliament approved five articles of the strategic action plan for the sustainable security of the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. One of the key approved items is the prohibition of transit of equipment owned by the US, Israel, and hostile countries through the Strait of Hormuz. The review of other articles of the plan has been postponed to future sessions.

About 250 workers at Madkoush Steel Company in Bandar Abbas were dismissed by the employer. The company is located in the special economic zone of mineral and metal industries of the Persian Gulf. The layoffs have recently taken place.

Mohsen Rezaei was appointed as the representative of Mojtaba Khamenei in the Supreme National Security Council. He was also assigned as the secretary of the council by Masoud Pezeshkian. The Supreme National Security Council is one of the most important decision-making bodies in security and foreign policy.

The audio version of the Titraval program with Niusha Saremi has been released. The program mentions changes in commanders and the return of Taeb by the order of Mojtaba Khamenei. The topic of security reorganization in Iran is also discussed.

Jaber Rajabi said that Mojtaba Khamenei's recent appointments and increased activities may indicate his more public presence. He added that appointing Hossein Taeb as the commander of Basij shows planning to rely on a core group of supporters. These developments could lead to an increased role of Basij in the power structure.

At least 9 protest gatherings were held today, Monday, 19 Mordad, by retirees of telecommunications and the Steel Retirement Fund of Isfahan in various cities. These protests continued for the third consecutive day. The cities of Bijar, Arak, Ahvaz, Isfahan, Kermanshah, Sanandaj, Ardabil, and Tehran hosted these protests.

Manchester United's negotiations to hire Jose Mourinho as Sir Alex Ferguson's successor lasted for weeks and initially reached an agreement. However, Mourinho withdrew due to a promise to Chelsea and family reasons. Subsequently, Manchester United appointed David Moyes as the new manager.

Hossein Ali Hajideligani criticized the government's economic performance in a parliamentary session, stating the government lacks an economic plan and called for the formation of an economic war room. He linked the rise in prices of essential goods, cars, and exchange rates to government policies. He also expressed concern that the Caspian Sea convention would reduce Iran's share.

Brent crude oil prices in the market surpassed $84. The reason for this increase is cited as the uncertain situation in the Strait of Hormuz. American officials told Axios that eight million barrels of oil are exported daily from the Strait of Hormuz in coordination with the US military.

Shayan Mohammadi remains in an uncertain detention status in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz after 22 days of arrest. His case is still unresolved, and he is denied contact and visitation with his family. This information was confirmed by a source close to his family.

Mehdi Taj announced that the new season of Iranian football league will be held with spectators. After the National Iranian Revolution in December 1404, matches were mostly held without spectators. No matches in Tehran had spectators.

Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the 15-point peace plan led by the US and stated that the Israeli army will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is truly disarmed. He also said that as long as he is prime minister, no independent Palestinian state will be established in Gaza or the West Bank. Meir Javdanfar explained Israel's opposition to a Palestinian state is due to the experience of withdrawing from Gaza and its transformation into a base for armed groups.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry stated that reopening the Strait of Hormuz depends on the lifting of the US naval blockade. The parliament approved the general framework of a plan to ensure the sustainable security of the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. This plan aims to turn the Islamic Republic's policies regarding the strait into law.

Donald Trump emphasized US Navy control over the Strait of Hormuz, stating they have established an unbreakable blockade like a steel wall, denying ship entry to Iran while keeping the route open for others. He also announced mine-clearing in the strait and described Iran as bankrupt with no money.

The International Atomic Energy Agency will soon remove the remaining nuclear materials from Syria's Site 99 following secret agreements between the Trump administration, Israel, and Syria. These materials are insufficient for nuclear weapons but raised concerns about use in a dirty bomb. An agreement between Damascus and the agency for safe transfer of these materials was signed three weeks ago.

Morad Vaisi said Mojtaba Khamenei considers the future uprising of the people as the most significant threat to the Islamic Republic. Basij is at the forefront of suppressing protests. Hossein Taeb has been appointed as a trusted person at the head of Basij.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic has demanded compensation in negotiations. He said the United States can also claim compensation for damages caused by the Islamic Republic. Trump referred to incidents such as the USS Cole and the protesters killed in recent months.

Verbal tensions between Iranian and US officials have increased amid more complex negotiations. Donald Trump responded to Iran's compensation request by stating that Iran should pay for damages over the past 50 years and the killing of protesters. This report was published by Niloufar Mansouri from Iran International.
